name: Japanese modern craft product
summary: Japanese household objects of bamboo, paper, clay, iron and plain wood: the mingei idea of beauty in ordinary things, joined to post-war modern design and light industrial series.

philosophy.core_thesis: A useful object made with skill from a local material is beautiful without ornament; the maker's hand and the material leave the only decoration.
design_principles: Use a local material of plain character: bamboo, washi paper, clay, cast iron, cotton or ash.
Leave the mark of the hand in view: throwing rings, a brush stroke, a weave or a tool cut.
Join parts without hidden fixings: a joint, a lashing or a single brass rod stays in view.
Draw a form from use, in a pure curve or a straight line, with no applied pattern.
Keep colours to the natural tones of the material, with indigo, iron brown and unbleached white.
Let the object leave space round it: a small body in an open, empty room.
Make each object so that it improves with use, and mend it with the same craft.
Join the craft method to a light series, so that a household can own the object.
anti_patterns: Perfectly even machine finish with no trace of the hand
Dragon, wave and cherry blossom motifs as souvenir decoration
Heavy dark lacquer on every surface
Crowded shelves and many small ornaments

form.geometry: Pure curves and straight lines: the circle, the arc, the square and the plane, in thin sheet, rod and woven strip.
form.silhouette: A small, calm outline with open space round it; a stool of two bent shells, a round lantern or a plain bowl.
form.edges: Soft radius of 3 to 15 mm on wood and clay; a thin edge on paper and bamboo.
form.proportion: A low table is 30 to 40 cm high; a stool is 35 to 40 cm high; a paper lantern is 30 to 60 cm across.
form.ornament: None applied. The only pattern is the weave of cane, the rings of the potter's wheel and the grain of the wood.
rules: Each object has 1 to 3 parts and no applied pattern.
Each joint is a lashing, a peg, a tenon or a single metal rod in view.
Clay carries the marks of the wheel and a matte, earth-coloured glaze.
Paper and bamboo parts keep the natural fibre in view.
A colour other than the material tone is indigo, iron black or white.

materials.rule: Plant fibre, wood and clay make about 80% of the visible surface; metal is small and dark.

finish.gloss: 0–10 GU on all main surfaces; 20–40 GU on glazed clay
finish.patina: The style values age: oiled wood darkens, paper yellows, iron takes a dark skin, and a repair is a mark of care.

hardware.section: Wire and rod 3–8 mm; handles and bails of cast iron 10–15 mm
hardware.joints: Peg and wedge, lashing with cord, or a single brass rod through two bent shells; always in view.
hardware.handles: A cut notch, a bamboo or cane loop, or a plain wooden peg of 20 mm.
hardware.switches_and_taps: A small square plate of white porcelain or plain wood; a simple cylindrical tap in dark metal.

palette.strategy: The tone of the material: paper white, ash and bamboo, with indigo and iron brown as the only deep colours.

processes: hand throwing and wood-fired glazing of clay
making of washi paper from bark fibre
bending of plywood in a mould
manufacture.scale: Workshops and village potteries of a few craftspeople, and short industrial series of a few thousand pieces for a national market.
manufacture.signs: Throwing rings in clay, a bamboo lashing, a visible brass rod, a slight irregular glaze and the unbleached colour of paper.

objects.form: deep square bath of solid wood
small square plate of white porcelain
round paper lantern on a thin rib frame
low chest with flush, pull-less drawers and a notch grip
indigo-dyed floor cushion with a slub weave
low, plain table on four square legs
hand-thrown rice bowl with an iron-brown glaze

emotion.target_response: Quiet respect: the object shows the hand that made it and asks the user to slow down.

use_cases: objects for a calm, craft-led interior
a still life of bowls, paper and wood
product briefs for a craft collection
a hardware schedule for a Japanese-influenced flat
avoid_when: The brief asks for a glossy, high-tech or colourful object.
The brief asks for ornament or a decorative pattern.

modifiers.how: Swap bamboo and paper for oiled teak and oak, and add wool and a paper cord seat.
Replace the marks of the hand with a grid, white plastic and brushed aluminium.
Keep the plain form but use a precise machine finish and a quiet grey and white palette.

ornament_level.note: A trace of pattern comes only from the weave or the throwing rings.

era_blend.note: A contemporary piece may quote the method with a machine.
